capabilities.text: Send nurse notes from Epic Cogito to CareTrack
capabilities.quote: We’re only bridging the gap between Epic Cogito and CareTrack, avoiding double data entry

capabilities.text: Extract patient identifiers (MRN, encounter ID) from FHIR Observation resource
capabilities.quote: We’ll extract these from the FHIR Observation resource in Epic using the `identifier` and `valueString` fields.

capabilities.text: Send full note text and patient identifiers to CareTrack
capabilities.quote: CareTrack must receive the full note text and the patient identifiers—specifically the MRN (Medical Record Number) and the encounter ID

capabilities.text: Ward manager views notes in CareTrack for daily audits
capabilities.quote: The ward manager needs to see the full note text and timestamp to verify handover completeness during daily audits.

capabilities.text: Night shift nurse views notes in CareTrack for care planning
capabilities.quote: The night shift nurse needs to see the note text, the nurse’s name, and the timestamp to inform their care plan.

capabilities.text: Send note as JSON payload with specific fields (text, author, authoredOn, mrn, encounterId)
capabilities.quote: We’ll send the note as a JSON payload containing `text`, `author`, `authoredOn`, `mrn`, and `encounterId`—no additional metadata.

capabilities.text: Azure Functions for processing notes
capabilities.quote: I’ll build it using Azure Functions with C# and the Azure App Service for hosting

capabilities.text: Azure App Service for hosting
capabilities.quote: I’ll build it using Azure Functions with C# and the Azure App Service for hosting

capabilities.text: Azure AD for Single Sign-On (SSO)
capabilities.quote: leveraging Azure AD for SSO.

capabilities.text: C# and .NET stack for development
capabilities.quote: I’ll stick with C# and .NET for consistency, faster development, and better maintainability.

capabilities.text: HIPAA compliance for data handling
capabilities.quote: This data is subject to HIPAA, as it contains protected health information (PHI) including MRN, encounter ID, and clinical note text.

capabilities.text: Encryption at rest and in transit (TLS 1.3)
capabilities.quote: We’ll enforce encryption at rest and in transit (TLS 1.3)

capabilities.text: Restrict access via Azure AD roles with least privilege
capabilities.quote: restrict access via Azure AD roles with the principle of least privilege

capabilities.text: Azure App Service in a dedicated virtual network with private endpoints
capabilities.quote: The Azure App Service will run in a dedicated virtual network with private endpoints for Epic and CareTrack integrations

capabilities.text: Azure Monitor with audit trails for data flows (version 1: 90-day retention)
capabilities.quote: For version one, we’ll implement audit trails only for the core data flow—specifically, successful note sends to CareTrack—and store those logs in Azure Monitor with a retention of 90 days.

capabilities.text: Azure AD authentication for CareTrack webhook
capabilities.quote: I’ll keep Azure AD for the webhook—CareTrack already supports OAuth 2.0 with Azure AD

capabilities.text: 90-day secret rotation policy for Azure AD client secret
capabilities.quote: set up a secrets rotation policy to refresh the client secret every 90 days.

capabilities.text: Automatic note sending from Epic to CareTrack upon Save and Close
capabilities.quote: Yes, the note must send automatically when the nurse clicks “Save and Close” in Epic Cogito

capabilities.text: Toast notification in Epic confirming note send (MRN, timestamp, green checkmark)
capabilities.quote: The message will appear as a toast notification in Epic, showing the patient’s MRN, the timestamp, and a green checkmark.

capabilities.text: Night nurse sees a green 'Received' badge in CareTrack for successfully ingested notes
capabilities.quote: So we’ll add a “Received” badge in green if the note was successfully ingested via the bridge

capabilities.text: Night nurse sees a grey 'Pending' badge for notes not yet received
capabilities.quote: She should see a grey "Pending" badge with a clock icon—indicating the note is expected but not yet received.

capabilities.text: Silent alert to monitoring dashboard if note remains pending for 5 minutes
capabilities.quote: If it remains pending after 5 minutes, the system will trigger a silent alert to the bridge’s monitoring dashboard

capabilities.text: Log failure in Azure Monitor after second send attempt fails
capabilities.quote: If the second attempt fails, the note is logged in Azure Monitor with a failure reason (e.g., timeout, 401, malformed payload)

capabilities.text: Send Teams alert to IT incident channel after second send attempt fails
capabilities.quote: and a Teams alert is sent to the IT incident channel.
